rootCause: Web derived a started thread's locked provider from session.providerName before the canonical thread provider.

The fixture carries the provider display name Codex and the canonical provider instance codex. ProviderDriverKind is intentionally open and permits mixed case, so Codex passed schema validation but matched no live provider entry whose driver kind is codex.
The Web Composer therefore selected t3code_no_provider and rendered disabled while Lynx correctly rendered GPT-5.6-Sol and an idle Composer.
productLossClosed: Web now resolves persisted provider instance ids through the live ServerProvider snapshot before deriving the started-thread driver lock.
The canonical thread provider wins over legacy session.providerName, while providerName remains a fallback for legacy sessions without a resolvable instance.
Custom provider instances resolve to their owning driver kind and missing instances do not silently substitute another provider.
evidenceBoundary: Dark and light Browser captures use the same immutable rich completed snapshot, 1280x820 viewport, committed Web and Lynx-for-Web bundles, and the committed completed-provider gate.

The gate requires a non-empty equal model label, equal Composer state, equal placeholder, and equal control ids. Both themes report GPT-5.6-Sol, idle, the canonical prompt placeholder, and model/model-option/runtime/interaction controls.

Fresh exact-bundle Native dark and light runs select the same completed thread, preserve providerName Codex with providerInstanceId codex, use main transport, open the real checkpoint diff through a measured tap, report zero renderer errors, and dispose isolated state.

The Web-only provider update notification and Native provider-health banner are separate product/session states. They are excluded from this lock attribution and the existing rich transcript geometry and material residuals remain unchanged.
